problems.description: An advanced persistent threat (APT) group infiltrates the enterprise network through a spear-phishing campaign targeting executives. Once inside, the attackers utilize custom malware to maintain persistence, gather intelligence, and slowly exfiltrate sensitive data over several months without detection. The attack employs lateral movement tactics to access high-value assets and evade standard security measures.
risk_reduction: Implement network segmentation to limit lateral movement opportunities
Use advanced threat detection systems capable of identifying anomalous behavior
Conduct regular security audits and penetration testing to uncover vulnerabilities

problems.description: Attackers exploit misconfigurations in cloud security groups that allow inbound traffic from anywhere. They target servers hosting sensitive data and deploy ransomware, encrypting data and demanding ransom. Resources are improperly sized, causing over-provisioning of permissions for service accounts, enabling attackers to deploy malicious workloads.
risk_reduction: Enforce strict security configurations and regularly review security group settings
Conduct automated compliance checks against best practice benchmarks
Implement a least privilege policy for cloud service accounts and apply role-based access controls

problems.description: A threat actor gains physical access to edge computing devices used in a smart building environment. They install hardware implants that allow them to capture sensitive data, manipulate device functionality, and turn the devices into attack vectors for further network penetration. This physical attack goes unnoticed until significant damage occurs.
risk_reduction: Install tamper-proof enclosures and secure all physical locations with access control systems
Conduct regular physical security audits of edge device locations
Use logging and monitoring systems to detect unauthorized access to critical infrastructure
